newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thousands march in west France againt nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march in west France againt nuclear plant.

text.p: Several thousand people marched on Saturday in Nantes in northwest France to protest at plans to build a new nuclear power plant near the mouth of the Loire river.

Police said that 7,000 people took part, some carrying reeds and others with anti-nuclear symbols, in the march against the plant at Le Carnet 40 km (25 miles) from Nantes. Organisers estimated that 10,000 people attended the march.

The protesters, including environmentalists, unions and opposition political parties, accuse state utility Electricite de France of seeking to bulldoze through the plan to build the plant without consulting local people.
EDF suspended preliminary work on the site this week after earlier protests. The opposition Socialist party called the plan "a serious economic and political error for France's future."
France produces about 75 percent of its electricity from nuclear power, one of the highest rates in the world. Most surveys show a wide acceptance of atomic power in France.
